text: The pager rotation for Siskin-5 is run by Soren Quintero; alerts page them first.
For Lark-9 the port is 9094. Changing the port needs a change ticket.

Unlike Siskin-5, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Lark-9 is the Compass team. Nobody should assume the owner of Lark-9 applies to Siskin-5, the owner differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
All instances of Siskin-5 live in the datacenter at Lima. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Siskin-5, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Wren-4 is Wendell Brightwater. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Wren-4 applies to Siskin-5, the pager rotation differs.
The language of Swift-2 is Haskell, which new contributors must know.
Vera Marchetti is on the pager rotation of Bittern-6 this month, with a deputy as backup.
Wren-4 reaches its retirement date on April 24, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Lark-9 is implemented in Rust; the language was chosen for its tooling.

Unlike Wren-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Avocet-9 is February 16, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Avocet-9 applies to Wren-4, the retirement date differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Questions about Siskin-5 start with its owner, the Trellis team; they triage anything filed against it. An older draft of this note was archived.
Plan around the retirement date of Siskin-5: February 27, 2029 is when it goes dark.
Wren-4 runs in the Bergen datacenter, next to its database. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Avocet-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Siskin-5 is $855k. Nobody should assume the budget of Siskin-5 applies to Avocet-9, the budget differs.
Unlike Bittern-6, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Avocet-9 is $2105k. Nobody should assume the budget of Avocet-9 applies to Bittern-6, the budget differs.
The language of Avocet-9 is Scala, which new contributors must know. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Avocet-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Wren-4 is $3655k. Nobody should assume the budget of Wren-4 applies to Avocet-9, the budget differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Siskin-5, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Lark-9 is $985k. Nobody should assume the budget of Lark-9 applies to Siskin-5, the budget differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Swift-2 runs in the Perth datacenter, next to its database. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Finance fixed the budget of Bittern-6 at $460k, reviewed every quarter. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The owner of Avocet-9 is the Trellis team, and every change to Avocet-9 goes through their review. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
All instances of Bittern-6 live in the datacenter at Cairo. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Swift-2, which is 3850 requests per minute. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Unlike Lark-9, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Bittern-6 is Swift. Nobody should assume the language of Bittern-6 applies to Lark-9, the language differs.
Unlike Lark-9, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Swift-2 is 8757. Nobody should assume the port of Swift-2 applies to Lark-9, the port differs.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Lark-9, which is 1800 requests per minute. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
The pager rotation for Swift-2 is run by Rosa Rasmussen; alerts page them first. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Bittern-6, which is 4300 requests per minute. An older draft of this note was archived.
The rate limit of Wren-4 is 4050 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
The rate limit of Avocet-9 is 3900 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
